definition: In neuroscience and machine learning, three-factor learning is the combination of Hebbian plasticity with a third modulatory factor to stabilise and enhance synaptic learning.
details: This third factor can represent various signals such as reward, punishment, error, surprise, or novelty, often implemented through neuromodulators.

explainer.lead: Three-factor learning combines Hebbian plasticity with a third modulatory factor to stabilize and enhance synaptic learning. It matters because it links biological learning rules to machine learning.

tiers.eli5: Two neurons getting used to firing together is only part of the story; a third signal—like a reward or a surprise—tells the connection whether to strengthen or hold back.
tiers.practitioner: Researchers implement the third factor as a reward, error, surprise, or novelty signal, often via neuromodulators, to gate when plasticity happens. A pitfall is that the modulatory signal must be timed with the Hebbian event, or learning is misattributed.
tiers.paperLevel: The combination of Hebbian plasticity with a third modulatory factor representing signals such as reward, punishment, error, surprise, or novelty, often implemented through neuromodulators. The description gives no single formula or quantified limit.

explainer.example: In a reward-driven setting, a synapse strengthens only when presynaptic and postsynaptic activity coincide and a reward signal is present, so the same activity without reward leaves the connection largely unchanged.
